channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Gold bears target $4,000 as stronger US Dollar and Fed rate-hike bets weigh
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) falls on Wednesday, revisiting the seven-month low touched earlier this month as hawkish Federal Reserve (Fed) expectations and the resulting strength in the US Dollar (USD) keep the precious metal under pressure.

item.title: Euro: Testing 1.1300 risk grows against US Dollar – ING
item.description: ING’s Francesco Pesole highlights that EUR/USD has been pressured by an equity sell-off and weak German PMIs, reinforcing a US-EU growth divergence narrative. He notes a wider EUR:USD two-year swap differential and a renewed Dollar risk premium.

item.title: Gold Price Forecast: XAU/USD heads for the $4,000 level as US Dollar marches higher
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) extends losses for the second consecutive day on Wednesday as the US Dollar Index (DXY) surges to 13-month highs near 102.00. The precious metal has breached the 4,100 line and is heading to retest Year-to-date lows, at $4,023, and probably also the $4,000 psychological level.

item.title: SNB’s Tschudin: Ready to intervene in FX market if necessary
item.description: The comments from Swiss National Bank (SNB) policymaker Petra Tschudin released during the European trading session on Wednesday indicate that medium-term inflation pressures remain unchanged and the central bank is ready to intervene in the FX market if necessary.

item.title: Indian Rupee declines amid hawkish Fed bets, RBI pushes back rate hike fears
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) trades lower against the US Dollar (USD) on Wednesday, with the USD/INR pair rising to near 94.85. The pair gains as the US Dollar posts a fresh annual high amid firm expectations that the Federal Reserve (Fed) will deliver at least two interest rate hikes this year.

item.title: Strait of Hormuz talks begin as Gulf states oppose transit fees
item.description: Discussions on the future of the Strait of Hormuz could soon gain momentum. According to Reuters, Qatar's Prime Minister is in Muscat on Wednesday to initiate, alongside Oman, a dialogue process involving Iran, the Gulf states and Iraq on the reopening and future operation of the strategic waterway.

item.title: NZD/USD Price Forecast: Kiwi hits fresh YTD lows below 0.5650 as the US Dollar soars
item.description: The New Zealand Dollar (NZD) is failing to find a bottom as rising hopes of monetary tightening by the US Federal Reserve (Fed) and dismal market mood are boosting the safe-haven US Dollar (USD) on Wednesday.

item.title: Euro edges lower vs Yen as German sentiment, ECB caution meet Japan intervention fears
item.description: EUR/JPY edges lower on Wednesday, trading around 183.55 at the time of writing, down 0.17%, as investors assess the impact of improving economic sentiment in Germany against rising intervention risks in Japan’s foreign exchange market.

item.title: Australian Dollar: Valuation gap and downside risks – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale analysts note AUD/USD remains under pressure, converging on the 0.69 area and the March–April trough near 0.6833, despite a sharp tightening in the 2‑year spread to 39bp.

item.title: Euro: Yield gap drives downside risk against US Dollar – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Lee Hardman notes that EUR/USD has broken below its long-held 1.1400–1.1800 range as diverging ECB and Fed policy expectations weigh on the Euro. Softer Euro-zone data and easing energy prices are reducing pressure on the ECB to hike further, while the Fed is priced for multiple hikes.

item.title: Silver Price Forecasts: XAG/USD licks its wounds above $61.00 amid a strong US Dollar
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) nurses marginal losses, trading a few cents above the $61.00 level on Wednesday’s European trading session.

item.title: Silver price today: Silver falls, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Silver prices (XAG/USD) fell on Wednesday, according to FXStreet data. Silver trades at $61.15 per troy ounce, down 0.72% from the $61.60 it cost on Tuesday.

item.title: US Dollar: Strength reflected in year-end forecast revisions – OCBC
item.description: OCBC’s Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong highlight that recent AI-related equity weakness has boosted safe-haven demand and supported the Dollar.

item.title: AUD/USD Price Forecast: More downside looks likely towards 0.6830
item.description: The AUD/USD pair is down 0.28% to near 0.6900 during the European trading session on Wednesday, the lowest level seen in over two months.

item.title: Oil: Market questions pace of Gulf supply recovery – ING
item.description: ING analysts Warren Patterson and Ewa Manthey note that Oil prices are grinding lower as flows from the Persian Gulf gradually recover, with ICE Brent down over 1%. They argue the sell-off looks overdone given a still-tightening market and limited recovery in Strait of Hormuz volumes.

item.title: United States Dollar Index holds above 101.50 on hawkish Fed bets
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY), which measures the value of the US Dollar (USD) against six major currencies, continues its winning streak for the third successive day and is reaching a fresh 13-month high of 101.60 during the European hours on Wednesday.

item.title: British Pound: Head and shoulders signals gains against Euro – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale’s technical analysts observe EUR/GBP has formed a lower peak around 0.8690 below its 200‑day moving average and is pulling back towards the neckline of a Head and Shoulders pattern.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Intervention risk tempers downside against US Dollar – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Lee Hardman highlights that USD/JPY is trading near recent highs but remains capped below the July 2024 peak of 161.95 as intervention risks rise.

item.title: Hungarian Forint: Faster easing path signalled – Standard Chartered
item.description: Standard Chartered’s Saabir Salad notes that the National Bank of Hungary (MNB) cut the base rate by 25 bps to 6.00%, in line with expectations, and delivered notably dovish forward guidance.

item.title: Dow Jones futures slip on hawkish sentiment surrounding Fed outlook
item.description: Dow Jones futures fall by 0.13%, trading near 52,000 during the European hours on Wednesday. However, S&P 500 futures are up by 0.13% near 7,450, while Nasdaq 100 futures advance 0.36%, trading near 29,770 at the time of writing.

item.title: Euro extends downfall against US Dollar amid firm Fed hike bets
item.description: The Euro (EUR) extends its losing streak against the US Dollar (USD) for the third trading day on Wednesday, trading 0.25% lower at around 1.1350 during the European session.

item.title: Gold languishes near two-week low as USD hits 13-month top on Fed hike bets
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) maintains its offered tone below the $4,100 mark through the first half of the European session, within striking distance of a nearly two-week low touched earlier this Wednesday.

item.title: Australian Dollar: Sharp selloff opens 0.6835 risk against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann highlight an abrupt 1.22% plunge in AUD/USD to 0.6908, leaving the pair deeply oversold but still biased lower. Intraday, they see potential for a brief break below 0.6900 while expecting it not to hold.

item.title: WTI Oil drifts below $72.00 as Iran eases the grip on the Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Crude Oil prices keep trending lower, with the US benchmark West Texas Intermediate (WTI) barrel extending its decline below the $72.00 line on Wednesday, and reaching its lowest level since the UA and Israel attacked Iran in late February.

item.title: US Dollar: Safe-haven bid and Fed support – ING
item.description: ING’s Francesco Pesole notes that the US Dollar (USD) is benefiting from equity market turmoil and hawkish Federal Reserve (Fed) commentary, with safe-haven demand reinforcing its strength.

item.title: Germany’s IFO Business Climate Index improves to 85.6 in June, as expected
item.description: The German IFO Institute Business Climate Index improves to 85.6 in June, as expected, from 85.0 in May, revised higher from 84.9.

item.title: US equities: Tech-led setback weighs on indexes – Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank strategists note that United States (US) equities experienced a classic risk-off session, with major indexes pressured by a sharp sell-off in chipmakers. The NASDAQ dropped more than the S&P 500 as semiconductor weakness dragged broader benchmarks lower.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD rebounds toward $62.00 after hitting fresh six-month lows
item.description: XAG/USD holds ground after registering over 5% losses in the previous day, trading around $61.70 per troy ounce during the European hours on Wednesday.

item.title: Forex Today: US Dollar extends rally to fresh 13-month high
item.description: Here is what you need to know on Wednesday, June 24:

item.title: Singapore Dollar: Pressured with stronger US Dollar – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank notes USD/SGD rose 0.3% to 1.2970 and has been grinding higher since mid-June on broader Dollar strength.
